decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up right-arm approach to the yellow nut; gradual downward wrist rotation and clearance lift, with left arm parked.
Align downward right gripper above the yellow nut using calibrated head geometry; stop above grasp height to inspect centering.
Descend open gripper toward yellow nut at measured approach XY; inspect wrist centering before closure.
Fine-center yellow nut from wrist view, close fully, then lift gently to check that the nut is retained.
Yellow nut visibly retained. Lift for clearance and carry it above the yellow screw, keeping right-arm elbow-up and gripper closed.
Lower the retained yellow nut toward the screw, stopping near insertion height to refine alignment from the wrist image.
Fine alignment: bring yellow nut slightly toward the visible shaft center while maintaining the closed grasp; descend only 3 mm.
Shaft appears centered in yellow nut. Apply a controlled clockwise tightening stroke with a small axial advance, keeping the grasp closed.
Correct the remaining lateral shaft offset revealed by wrist rotation, then finish a short clockwise stroke with gentle axial advance.
Open the right gripper and reset wrist yaw for another tightening stroke; observe whether the yellow nut remains seated.
Yellow nut remains on the shaft after release. Recenter slightly, regrasp, and apply another clockwise stroke with a small downward thread advance.
The yellow shaft is now centered and much deeper in the nut. Release and reset yaw without lifting the seated nut for a final tightening stroke.
Regrasp yellow nut, apply a final clockwise stroke with 1.8 mm axial advance, and release to inspect seating.
Yellow nut remains seated with shaft near its top. Lift clear with gripper open, reset wrist yaw, and approach the red nut on the right.
Move above the red nut at calibrated head-image XY, descending only to a pregrasp height with the right gripper open.
Center the red nut using the wrist view, descend to the grasp height, and close the right gripper without moving the left arm.
Lift the red nut clear and carry it above the matching red screw, keeping the right gripper fully closed and the wrist vertical.
Red nut is retained. Lower toward insertion height while correcting the leftward shaft offset visible in the wrist camera.
Fine-center the red nut over the visible shaft, then begin a slow clockwise insertion stroke while maintaining the closed grasp.
Red shaft and nut appear coaxial. Continue a slow clockwise stroke with 4 mm of gentle axial advance, checking engagement next.
Red nut may be tilting under the grasp. Release and reset the wrist without further axial advance, then inspect its settled alignment.
Red nut has settled upright around the shaft. Apply one final controlled clockwise stroke with minimal axial advance, then release.
Red nut remains seated after release. Lift clear, reset right wrist yaw, and approach the blue nut for a middle-table handover.
Descend open right gripper toward the blue nut, with a small wrist-image centering correction; stop above final grasp height.
Fine-center and descend to blue-nut grasp height, then close the right gripper; retention will be checked before the handover.
Lift the blue nut and begin carrying it toward the middle. Prepare the left arm in an elbow-up approach, remaining well left of the right arm.
Carry blue nut to the midline and begin lowering for table handover. Left arm completes its downward orientation but waits on its own side with clearance.
Set the blue nut onto the middle of the table, release, and lift the right gripper away while the left waits clear.
Blue nut is on the table. Withdraw the right arm to its own side while moving the left gripper above the midline nut with ample separation.
Lower the left gripper toward the blue nut for handover pickup. Return the empty right arm toward home gradually without changing its elbow-up branch.
Fine-center and grasp the blue nut with the left arm, then make a small retention-check lift. Complete the empty right arm's gradual return home.
Blue nut is retained in the left gripper. Lift to clearance and carry it left toward the matching screw; keep the right arm parked open.
Bring the retained blue nut over the left-side screw and lower to a cautious pre-insertion height for wrist-image alignment.
Corrected tensor; prior call executed nothing. Fine-center the blue nut, then apply a short clockwise insertion stroke; right arm stays parked.
Correct the remaining blue-shaft offset revealed by the rotated wrist view, then complete a short clockwise stroke with gentle axial advance.
Blue nut appears centered on the shaft. Release and reset left wrist yaw for the next tightening stroke without lifting the nut.
Blue nut tilted after release rather than staying seated. Lift the open left gripper clear and let it settle before planning recovery.
Recover the tilted blue nut: center the left gripper over its displaced body, regrasp, and lift gently away from the screw for inspection.
Previous lift did not retain the tilted nut. Reopen, descend lower around its body with a small centering correction, and close for another recovery grasp.
Blue nut has fallen flat beside the screw. Reopen and clear the screw, then approach the nut's new table position for a fresh upright grasp.
Descent was obstructed near the screw. Lift clear and change left gripper yaw so the fingers can approach the flat nut without contacting the adjacent shaft.
Previous chunk was rejected without movement. Start at the observed pose, lift in smaller increments, then begin the clearance yaw adjustment.
Continuity check narrowly rejected the stationary start. Use a submillimeter reconciliation step, then lift clear and begin a slower yaw adjustment.
Complete the vertical, alternate-yaw approach to the flat blue nut, stopping above grasp height to verify clearance from the screw.
Center the flat blue nut in the left wrist image, descend with the fingers clear of the screw, close, and make a small test lift.
The nut appears too far forward between the fingers. Reopen and shift away from the screw to center its body, then regrasp and lift for a retention check.
The blue nut is now visibly retained upright. Lift clear of the screw and move above it, allowing for the nut's offset within the grasp.
Lower the upright blue nut slowly toward the shaft without rotating yet; verify centering before threading.
Refine blue-nut axial alignment, then start a gentle clockwise stroke with small XY compensation for the nut's off-center grasp.
Blue shaft now appears deeply seated and centered. Release the nut and lift the open left gripper clear to verify that the assembly stays upright.
Blue assembly stays upright after release; all three pairs appear seated. Return both open grippers toward their origin poses while preserving elbow-up continuity.
Settle both open grippers at their original poses and observe whether the three upright assemblies remain stable.
Blue received a shorter final threading stroke than the other colors. Reapproach it with the left gripper open to inspect and, if needed, tighten further.
Closer view shows the blue shaft centered and nearly flush in its nut. Leave the stable assembly undisturbed and return the open left gripper along its approach path.
Make small origin-pose corrections, then hold both grippers open while observing the three stable color-matched assemblies.
